newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Bratsk aluminium workers to protest but not strike.
newsitem.headline: Bratsk aluminium workers to protest but not strike.

text.p: An unspecified number of workers at Russia's largest aluminium smelter, Bratsk, will show solidarity with nationwide protests planned for Thursday but will not disrupt output, Interfax news agency said on Wednesday.
It quoted the Mining and Metallurgical Trade Union, which in turn quoted Bratsk trade union deputy chairman Mihkail Gribachyov, as saying workers wanted to support protestors across the country.
Bratsk board member Yuri Shlaifshtein told Reuters earlier this month that the plant paid salaries on time.
About 20 million protesters, backed by Russia's communist opposition, are expected by union officials to protest on Thursday against massive backlogs in wages and pensions.
Bratsk has forecast its 1997 primary aluminium output to rise to 790,685 tonnes from 783,130 in 1996.
